_about.what: The wider world, attached to a grand campaign when it opens (src/campaign/world.ts). The history campaigns never see any of it: they keep the map of Europe. The provinces and seas themselves come from tools/build-geo-world.mjs (data/campaign/world.mjs, world-seas.json); this file holds what the rules add to them.
_about.nations: Countries that exist only on the wider map, in the same form as nations.json.
_about.home: What changes for a country of nations.json once its homeland is on the map. The United States is no longer a country beyond the map's edge that wakes in December 1941: it is there from the first day, neutral, with its factories on its own soil.
_about.follow: Dominions: each goes to war with whoever its mother country is at war with on the day the world is attached.
_about.corps: The armies standing at home on the first day: [nation, name, kind, divisions, province, options]. 'str' is the strength it starts at (a peacetime army is a cadre).
_about.fleets: Squadrons in home waters on the first day, in the form of navy.json.
_about.peace: The share of a great power's industry on war work while it is at peace, by month: [from month, share]. It stands in place of production.json's peaceIncome for that country. Once it is at war its factories work as any other's do.
_about.protector: Overseas ground beyond the old chart whose mother country falls does not go to the victor's hands across an ocean he cannot cross: it passes into the keeping of the first of these powers that is alive, lives by its ships and is at war with the victor.
_about.pairs: Trade agreements history had in 1939, added to trade.json's.
_about.order: Where the new countries stand in the order of play: after the countries of nations.json.
_about.idle: A computer-run staff whose homeland lies beyond the old chart, with no enemy on its side of the ocean, does not go on raising an army to stand on the quay: once this many of its field corps are at home it raises no more. (It has no routine yet for shipping an army across an ocean by itself; history's dated formations still arrive where history landed them.) A player's own staff is not bound by it.
_about.great: Great powers beside diplomacy.json's 'majors', once their homeland is on the map: left alone when the neutrals are dealt afresh, paid a great power's political capital and trade houses, and counted among the great powers of the last act.

corps: Third Army (2nd Division and 1st Cavalry Division)
